summary: The note describes how mobile technologies have transformed marketing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) as of late 2023. It follows Nairobi boutique Rafiki Fashions and its owner Caroline Mwangi, and cites other SMEs, experts and events to show the effects of mobile apps, messaging, social media, e-commerce, personalization and networking. It also notes challenges such as security and keeping up with technology, and says the future of SME marketing is mobile.
one_line: Mobile technology, from apps to messaging and social media, is reshaping SME marketing, illustrated by Nairobi's Rafiki Fashions and other businesses.
key_facts: Caroline Mwangi owns Rafiki Fashions, a small boutique in Nairobi, and noticed a shift in how customers discovered her clothes in early September 2023.
At a webinar on November 3, 2023, digital marketing expert David Sanders said nearly 70% of internet traffic now originates from mobile devices.
The COVID19 pandemic accelerated adoption of digital channels; lockdowns in early 2021 pushed Rafiki Fashions toward mobile marketing.
By mid-September 2023, Rafiki Fashions launched its own mobile app that showcases its fashion lines and lets customers virtually try on clothes.
Instant messaging apps like WhatsApp let small businesses send updates, promotions and quick customer service replies, bypassing costlier traditional marketing.
Michelle Li, a social media consultant, said at the SME Digital Forum on November 12, 2023 that Instagram and TikTok let businesses reach niche audiences with great precision.
Choco Delight, an artisanal chocolate shop, recorded a 30% increase in online sales after revamping its mobile e-commerce capabilities in late September 2023.
Green Solutions, a startup selling eco-friendly products, uses mobile data analytics to tailor and personalize its marketing campaigns.
Book-keeping apps, inventory management software and productivity tools on smartphones help SMEs coordinate marketing with other operations.
Challenges of mobile adoption include security concerns, making content mobile-friendly, and keeping up with rapidly changing technology.
TechSolve Advisory supports SMEs with tailored IT solutions and workshops.
Lydia Chen, an SME networking facilitator, points to exponential growth in industry connections made via mobile networking platforms since late 2023.
